clue.text: Folios in linked series followed by church singer

indicators.note: in tells us the folios abbreviation sits inside the word for a linked series

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things
FF is the standard abbreviation for folios

explanation.surface: Pages bound in a series come before a member of the church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' sounds like a chorister, but it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The finch in question is a common songbird, so it qualifies as a singer.

clue.text: English in defeat, attacked from all sides

indicators.note: in says the English abbreviation goes inside the word for defeat

parts.note: to best someone is to defeat them

explanation.surface: An English side, losing, finds itself under attack everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set upon on every side is the literal sense of this verb, meaning surrounded and harassed.

clue.text: Pelt with resemblance to furry pets?

definitions.text: Pelt with resemblance to furry pets?

parts.words: Pelt with resemblance to furry pets?
parts.note: pelt means pour down heavily, and the idiom for a heavy downpour pictures household animals falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Something furry that looks like a pet's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a noun meaning fur; it is the verb for torrential rain, and the fanciful idiom has animals tumbling down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a torrential downpour, which is what pelting rain is.

clue.text: Timeless occurrences getting old, nonetheless

indicators.note: Timeless tells us to drop the time abbreviation from the word for occurrences

parts.note: events are occurrences

explanation.surface: Things that happen outside time still grow old, all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' removes T from EVENTS, leaving EVENS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means despite that, a synonym of nonetheless.

clue.text: Small article, Napoleon's last in field where he died

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: in says the chosen letter goes inside the word for field

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field in poetic usage

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of Napoleon's name

explanation.surface: A small item about Napoleon's final days in the place where he died.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: 'he' is Napoleon, exiled to the South Atlantic island where he died in 1821.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon spent his final exile on this remote island and died there.

clue.text: Having reversed Scots' Yes for start of independence, bring round carriage

indicators.note: for says one piece takes the place of another inside the word for bring round

parts.note: to convince someone is to bring them round to your view

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of independence
Having reversed says the Scots word for yes is read backwards

parts.note: aye is the Scottish word for yes

explanation.surface: After the Scottish referendum's Yes is turned back, the push for independence must win people round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having reversed' turns AYE into EYA, which replaces the I in CONVINCE to give CONV-EYA-NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A conveyance is any means of transport, a vehicle or carriage.

clue.text: Opposing section of Fortean Times

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Disagreeing with part of a magazine about the paranormal.
explanation.walkthrough: Fortean Times is a British magazine about strange phenomena.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is the sense of this prefix used as a word, so opposed or opposing.

clue.text: Outwardly trustworthy knave or cur

indicators.note: Outwardly takes just the outside letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A rogue who looks honest on the outside is really a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' gives TY from trustworthy and KE from knave; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyke is a mongrel dog, which is what a cur is.

clue.text: Reliable worker's trip to west of island

indicators.note: in an across answer west is to the left, so the trip comes before the island

parts.note: a journey is a trip
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A dependable employee travels west of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in the definition stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a competent, dependable craftsman who has served an apprenticeship.

clue.text: First pair in Arabian Gulf to adopt one primitive style

indicators.note: First pair in picks the opening two letters of Arabian
to adopt means to take in, so the gulf word takes in the letter for one

parts.note: a chasm is a deep gulf
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The opening pair in the Arabian Gulf take on a single primitive style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabian Gulf' reads as one place, the sea, but the two words are used separately.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an old-fashioned expression or manner, a deliberately antique style.

clue.text: Young animal protecting the female's sweet little one

indicators.note: protecting says the young animal word wraps round the female pronoun

parts.note: a cub is a young animal such as a fox or bear
her is the female possessive

explanation.surface: A cub guarding its mother's adorable baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a chubby, angelic child, so an endearing little one.

clue.text: Arm supporter to smooth a Resistance fight's adversities

parts.note: a sling holds up an injured arm
to sand is to smooth a surface
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
the 's stands for 'is'; to row is to quarrel or fight, so fight is gives rows

explanation.surface: A sling for an injured arm helps smooth over the setbacks of a fight with the Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Hamlet's phrase for the misfortunes life throws at us.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakespearean phrase stands for life's misfortunes and hardships, i.e. adversities.

clue.text: Tease American about carbohydrate

indicators.note: about tells us the pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to rag is to tease

explanation.surface: Teasing an American about what they eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAGUS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars such as glucose and sucrose are simple carbohydrates.

clue.text: Those succeeding in exams, using technique of random strangers?

parts.note: people who pass tests are passers
by means using the method of, as in by hand

explanation.surface: Students who passed by means of making random guesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a looser definition: people who walk past are strangers chosen at random.
explanation.definitionFit: People walking by in the street are chance onlookers, strangers met at random.

clue.text: Remedy restricting virus's onset shown in graph

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the remedy word holds the first letter of virus

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

indicators.note: onset picks the first letter of virus

explanation.surface: A treatment that limits early spread of a virus, as plotted on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes flattening the curve of infections.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve is a line plotted on a graph, the thing shown in it.

clue.text: In a heavy defeat, oddly naive Dalek losing innards is hardly subdued

indicators.note: In says the following pieces go inside the words for a heavy defeat

parts.note: a licking is a thrashing or heavy defeat

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, signalling the letters of naive are rearranged
losing innards keeps only the outer letters of Dalek

explanation.surface: In a crushing defeat, a strangely innocent gutted robot is still full of fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but here it is an anagram signal; 'losing innards' strips the middle of the robot's name, and both results go after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means vigorously active, the opposite of being subdued.

clue.text: Foreign Office meeting awkward with attention concentrated

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the UK's Foreign Office
cussed means stubborn or awkward

explanation.surface: A Foreign Office meeting turned difficult with everyone paying close attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be focused, in this spelling, is to have one's attention concentrated on something.

clue.text: Crazy time among students

indicators.note: among says the time letter goes inside the students abbreviation

parts.note: NUS is the UK National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A mad period at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for mad, so crazy.

clue.text: Pounds invested in excitement with frantic reach for NHS business

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the pounds letter goes into the excitement word

parts.note: heat is passion or excitement
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

indicators.note: frantic signals the letters of reach are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Money is poured into a thrill as the state health service grabs wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's state-funded National Health Service; 'frantic' makes CARE after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: The NHS's work is providing medical treatment, so its business is caring for health.

clue.text: Shift tons at low cost

parts.note: to budge is to shift slightly

explanation.surface: Moving tons of goods cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget used as an adjective means cheap, i.e. at low cost, as in budget airline.

clue.text: Somehow miss nod or remark providing misleading information

indicators.note: Somehow tells us the letters of the following words are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Somehow you overlook a nod or a comment that gives the wrong impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from conjuring, means deception or obfuscation, so misleading information.

clue.text: Like certain devils since frenzy in Tennessee

indicators.note: in says the two pieces go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for Tennessee
as can mean since, as in as it was late
mania is frenzy

explanation.surface: Devilish behaviour arising from a frenzy in Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devils' sounds demonic but refers to the marsupial from the Australian island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous marsupial, so certain devils are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Very keen swimmer's back on Atlantic islands culling European type of seal?

indicators.note: back picks the final letter of swimmer
culling means removing, so the European letter is taken out of the islands

parts.note: the Azores are a Portuguese island group in the Atlantic
the harp seal is a species of seal

explanation.surface: A swimmer's back on Atlantic islands where a kind of seal is being culled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' and 'seal' paint a marine scene; the seal is just HARP, and 'on' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Razor-sharp means extremely sharp or keen, of a blade or a mind.

clue.text: Medieval Christian sect exists for emotional purification

parts.note: the Cathars were a heretical sect of medieval southern France
is means exists

explanation.surface: A medieval sect lives on as a source of cleansing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the release of pent-up emotion, a purging of feeling.

clue.text: Brew of endless green tea stops: put more juice in

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the tea word fills a gap in the rearranged letters
Brew of signals the letters are stirred up into a new order
endless says the last letter of green is cut off

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Making up a brew of green tea ceaselessly, someone tops up the power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final N, 'Brew of' turns the remaining four letters into REGE, and 'stops' sets the tea inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is slang for electrical power, so to recharge a battery is to put more power into it.

clue.text: Harass naughty German

parts.note: bad means naughty

explanation.surface: Pestering a misbehaving German.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester or harass them persistently.

clue.text: Wrap up in fall for a shock might be described thus

definitions.text: a shock might be described thus

indicators.note: in says the hushing word goes inside the believing word

parts.note: to buy a story is to fall for it
sh is a call to be quiet, wrap up meaning shut up

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet while being taken in by a shocking surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is not a fright but a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is thick and shaggy, the kind of hair one calls bushy.

clue.text: Theologian overwhelmed by abnormally large probability

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped by, so the theologian letters sit inside the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian swamped by enormous chances.
explanation.definitionFit: The odds are the likelihood or probability of something happening.
